implementation.summary: D23 scopes Knowledge Graph persistence, adapter access, HTTP dispatch and scheduler graph queries by workspace. It adds a real local composed ontology/graph/RQL journey with two workspaces, typed ontology persistence, neighbors, restart recovery and authorization negatives. P6 remains in_progress.

security_and_recovery.graph_scope: The real local composed test stores the same graph id with different objects in two workspaces and proves HTTP query/object/neighbor responses stay in the requested workspace. The graph store also scopes action replay identities by workspace.
security_and_recovery.ontology_scope: The same journey persists a typed ontology definition against a governed catalog revision, reads its version collection and exact version through the HTTP surface, and verifies the materialized graph survives server restart.
security_and_recovery.project_scope: CatalogAsset.project_id remains metadata only; the public catalog still has no independent project-level filter or authorization claim. This D22 limitation remains open and is not changed by D23.
security_and_recovery.provider_scope: RONIN_POSTGRES_TEST_DSN is absent and Docker does not provide a responsive daemon. No PostgreSQL operator, Docker worker or external provider was certified, and no mock was substituted.

limitations: The exact candidate sandbox has no .git metadata by design, so Git-dependent tests and repository status checks are not claimed from it; main checkout checks run separately.

Web node_modules and the web regression runtime are outside the candidate archive; the 7/7 result is a clean-server checkout-source regression bound to the candidate SHA, not a claim that node_modules is archived.
Static checks generated .mypy_cache/.ruff_cache before cleanup/regeneration; cleanup removed them before final verify and the scans were repeated on the clean manifest-bound sandbox.
